title: Close-area arena: seeded 2.5D A=>B simulator, published drone interface, truth scorer
summary: Small deterministic simulator that every close-area A=>B approach in the hub is compared in. Walled 20 x 20 m area, axis-aligned boxes and cylinders in three seeded layout families (random clutter, a U trap with its inside corner on the A-B line, a wall with one 0.5-0.9 m gap), exact signed distance and ray casts, a 0.1 m occupancy grid, and a guaranteed free path (4-connected BFS on the grid inflated by the 0.15 m vehicle radius, else resample). 50 Hz double-integrator vehicle with a 0.15 s first-order velocity lag and acceleration and speed limits, z held. Ray-cast range fan with noise and dropout. Planners only see the published Pose / RangeScan / Setpoint / Adapter interface, so they port to a real drone adapter unchanged; a pose_source hook lets later samples substitute a faulty estimator while scans and scoring stay on truth. Scorer: reached (0.3 m), collision (clearance < radius), stuck (< 0.2 m in 10 s), timeout, time to goal, min clearance, path length. Ships three planners to start from: straight (floor), freest_beam (reactive, in run_faults.py) and astar_esdf (A* + ESDF, known or unknown map, planners/astar_esdf.py); a VIO-like EKF with seeded faults (estimator.py, faults.py, run_faults.py); a flight-log scorer for sim or real logs (score_log.py, log_format.md); a CLI with summary tables, JSON results and a PNG plot written without matplotlib, a scipy EDT timing on a 2M-cell grid, and CONTRACT.md for later planners, estimators and safety filters. numpy + scipy; matplotlib only for score_log.py.
verified: ran 2026-11-09 with CPython 3.12.10 + numpy 2.5.4 / scipy 1.18.1 on an Apple M3 Max: run.py --planner straight --layouts 20 --seed 0 ran twice (once with --plot) with identical per-run scores, and once each with --family u_trap and --family narrow_gap (with --plot); bench_edt.py wrote results/edt_timing.json. Every number in README is from results/. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the venv, 1 skipped under plain python3 without numpy; it loads the folder as a package the way CONTRACT.md tells sibling samples to. checks.py wrote results/checks.json: the BFS rejects a 0.3 m gap and accepts 0.4 m, and the straight planner with the slow-down disabled collides in 60 % of the 20 random layouts, so the scorer's collision path fires. Layouts, vehicle and sensor are simulated; no SITL, no real drone, and templates/drone-adapter was not present in this checkout to diff the interface against. Follow-up 2026-11-09 (same M3 Max, macOS 26.6.2 arm64): templates/drone-adapter is now present in the checkout; the interface diff against it is not yet done. Cold setup measured: uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --no-cache --python .venv -r requirements.txt took 16.5 s wall (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2 wheels from PyPI; the CPython 3.12.10 interpreter was already on the machine). The first command then ran under sandbox-exec with all network access denied (curl to pypi.org failed in the same sandbox) and gave per-run scores identical to results/straight_random_0.json (timings excluded); that run's rewritten results files were restored. test_smoke.py: 1 passed in the fresh venv.
shows: Seeded 2.5D A=>B arena (random, U-trap, narrow-gap layouts) behind the published pose/ranges/send_setpoint interface, truth scorer, straight baseline, EDT timing
runtime: ~1.5 s per 20 layouts, EDT bench ~2 s
key_result: [straight baseline, 20 random layouts](README.md#results-ran-2026-11-09-apple-m3-max-cpython-31210-numpy-254-scipy-1181): reached 40 %, collision 0 %, stuck 60 %; 0 % reached on u_trap and narrow_gap; EDT 200x200x50 median 183 ms

readiness.limitation: Synthetic 2.5D point-mass arena on one M3 Max; setup needs network for PyPI wheels (16.5 s cold, interpreter already present); offline checked for the first command only; no SITL, no real drone, Linux not tested.
